page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n2.medium is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated physical cores providing 2 vCPUs, and 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the ecs.n2.medium sits on the lower end of the spectrum. In stress-ng testing, single-core performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25%, while multi-core performance is poor, placing in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests show a similar trend, with uncached large-block read and write speeds categorized in the bottom 10%. Passmark CPU and memory scores also rank in the bottom 10%, reflecting limited computational throughput for intensive tasks.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation but modest benchmark results, this instance offers a cost-efficient option for lightweight workloads that require predictable CPU access without high-performance demands. It is suitable for basic web serving, small database operations, and simple utility scripts. However, it is not recommended for memory-intensive applications, high-throughput database systems, or heavy parallel processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n2.medium is a general-purpose instance featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz, paired with 8.0 GB of RAM and no local storage. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, this x86_64 instance provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Benchmark data indicates limited performance, with stress-ng CPU and Passmark memory metrics ranking in the bottom 10% to 25% cohorts. Uncached memory read and write speeds are also low. Consequently, this instance is best suited for lightweight, non-intensive workloads such as basic web serving, small-scale database operations, and simple utility tasks where dedicated CPU allocation is required at a lower resource density.
